accuracy.evidence: Matches the topic statement (words combine into sentences; a sentence expresses a complete thought; produce and expand complete sentences) and the sources: a simple sentence needs a subject and a verb, a fragment lacks one of them, a where/when/how phrase expands a sentence without making a second one, and a written sentence is demarcated by a capital letter and a full stop (NC Year 1 grammar appendix). Every 'whole' card in the lab and sorter has a subject and a finite verb; every 'not finished' card lacks the subject or the verb, and its feedback names which.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets documented early-writing slips: a noun phrase taken as a sentence (prediction 'Is The dog a whole sentence?', The big red, m2), a verb phrase with no subject (jumps high, runs to the shop), a detail split off with its own full stop (challenge option 'The bee buzzes. In the garden.', m7), the belief that a longer sentence is two (grow-step prediction, m4), full stops placed early or at the start, and a lower-case opening letter.

lab_distinct.evidence: The mechanics belong to sentence building: a two-car word train that only couples into a sentence when it has a who car and a does car, a fragment sort where each unfinished bit explains its missing part, a gap-filling mend where wrong chips (the tree, big, fast, in the pond) are rejected because they are not the missing subject or verb, a detail-stretch that keeps the single full stop, and a capital-and-full-stop tap. Shingle gate passed against every flagship lab, including flag_nv (nouns and verbs) and flag_prep.

lab_teaches.evidence: Pupils discover the two-part rule by coupling cars (one car alone prompts 'Who runs?' or 'What does the cat do?'), test it by sorting and mending, find that adding where/when/how leaves one sentence, and finish with the written conventions. The step text then names each idea: whole idea, who, doing word, detail, capital letter, full stop.

predictions.evidence: Three locked predictions with tempting wrong options: 'Yes' for The dog being a whole sentence (the train refuses it), 'a full stop only' for what jumps high is missing (the mend step shows it needs a who), and 'Two sentences' after adding on the mat (the sentence strip shows one who, one doing word, one full stop).

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six rotating questions with eleven tagged messages: no doing word, no who, already has a who, already has a doing word, nothing missing, detail split into its own sentence, detail as a fragment, full stop too early, full stop at the start, lower-case start, and a missing full stop.

readability.evidence: Kid text is under the family limit of grade 5 with very short sentences and the concrete examples used in the lab (the dog runs, the cat sleeps on the mat); canvas labels are one to four words with emoji pictures, and every canvas action is repeated as a big button. Adult text is under grade 10 and uses the precise terms subject, verb, fragment, expand, capital letter and full stop.

no_filler.evidence: Passed the filler regex and the 12% duplicate gate against every lesson including Basic Nouns & Verbs and Question Words. Each kid paragraph adds one idea (whole idea, two parts, unfinished bits, expanding, capital and full stop); adult paragraphs give the curriculum terms, the say-it-aloud test, the common mistakes and the lab outline.

mobile.evidence: Checked iPhone and 360 px Android screenshots of every step in light and dark: three who cards and three does cards sit in two rows above the two-car train and full-stop box, the sort tray sits above two wide boxes, the mend picture, gap strip and three chips fit, the four detail chips fit in one row, and the three word boxes plus the end box fit. The young class gives 56 px buttons under the canvas.

accessibility.evidence: walk.cjs: every task completes with Show me on desktop and iPhone 13, the challenge shows, axe WCAG 2.1 AA is clean in both themes, no console errors. Every drag has a button route (who and does buttons, Whole/Not finished buttons, gap buttons, + detail buttons, capital and full-stop buttons) and the canvas aria-label states the sentence or what is missing after every move.
